items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is f3.
At depth 16 the engine rates Re2 at least 80 centipawns below 18.f3.

hints: Count what each side's pieces can reach on the kingside and in the centre; ask which pawn move would give your pieces more room.
The f2-pawn is the only pawn that can still advance to support a push on e4. Which pawn move prepares e4?
A pawn on the f-file steps one square forward.
items.explain: In a four-line search (the engine ranks its four best moves at once) at depth 16 the engine puts f3 first. At depth 16 the engine rates Re2 at least 80 centipawns below 18.f3. This is evidence for the game move, not proof that no other move works.

items.prompt: In the game, 30.Ba3 gave up a bishop and Black's queen took it on a3. What did Black's queen stop doing by going to a3?
options: It stopped defending the knight on f6
It stopped guarding the back rank

answer.class: It stopped defending the knight on f6
options: It stopped defending the knight on f6
It stopped guarding the back rank

claims.statement: After 30.Ba3 Qxa3 only one black piece (the king) defends the knight on f6; before the capture two did.

hints: Count the black pieces that defend the knight on f6 before 30.Ba3 and again after Qxa3.
The queen on e7 defended f6; on a3 it is far away.
items.explain: Before 30.Ba3 the queen and the king defended the knight on f6. After Qxa3 only the king does, which is what makes Nh5+ and Qxf6+ work. This is the deflection: the queen was drawn away from its defensive job.
